title: examples: refresh tool calling (single + parallel) w/ allowlist + better incomplete-args errors
author: Sabrina James
release_notes:
- Update Python tool-calling examples to match canonical streaming/tool semantics (single + parallel tools)
- Add safe tool dispatch pattern (explicit allowlist + argument validation)
- Improve error messages when tool args are partial/incomplete during streaming
commits: examples: add single-tool calling example w/ allowlist dispatch
examples: add parallel tool calling example w/ bounded concurrency
sdk: add ToolCallArgumentAccumulator helper + clearer errors
docs: update README snippet links + terminology (tools vs functions)
tests: add regression tests for partial tool args + unknown tool names
chore: ruff fixes and typing cleanup
body: Summary: This updates the Python SDK tool calling examples to match the canonical patterns we’re rolling out across SDKs/docs: (1) accumulate tool-call argument deltas safely, (2) dispatch tools via an explicit allowlist, and (3) show a parallel-tools flow with bounded concurrency. Motivation: We’ve had drift between docs/examples and current gateway semantics around tool_call deltas, and support volume around partial tool args (customers attempting to json.loads on every delta and getting noisy/opaque JSONDecodeErrors). This PR provides copy/paste runnable examples and adds helper utilities + tests so we don’t regress. Details: - Adds examples/tool_calling_single.py showing a single tool call end-to-end: stream response events, collect tool_call deltas into a per-call buffer, parse args only when the model indicates the tool call is finalized, validate expected keys, execute the tool, and send tool result back to the model. - Adds examples/tool_calling_parallel.py showing multiple tool calls in a single model turn, executed concurrently with a semaphore (max_concurrency configurable). The example intentionally demonstrates handling >1 tool call without assuming ordering of deltas. - Introduces ToolCallArgumentAccumulator (redwood/tooling/_tool_args.py) to centralize the tricky bits: mapping (tool_call_id -> accumulated args string), marking calls complete, and producing a structured error when the stream ends and args are incomplete. - Improves error reporting by raising IncompleteToolArgumentsError with: tool_call_id, tool_name, number of bytes received, and a short redacted tail snippet (last ~80 chars) to aid debugging without logging full user data. - Adds UnknownToolError when the model requests a tool name not in the allowlist; the example shows returning a safe tool error response rather than attempting to execute anything arbitrary. - Tests: adds regression coverage for partial JSON across multiple deltas, mixed interleaving of deltas from parallel tool calls, and unknown tool name handling. Notes/compat: These are examples + internal helper only; no changes to public client method signatures. The helper lives under redwood.tooling.* and is treated as internal (documented as such). How to run (examples): export REDWOOD_API_KEY=... then python examples/tool_calling_single.py and python examples/tool_calling_parallel.py. Both default to a small model in the catalog; override via REDWOOD_MODEL if needed. Related: ENG-2843 (Python example refresh), ENG-2848 (tool-call delta semantics alignment), PM-612 (terminology), SUP-18421 (partial args + disconnect symptoms). Review notes / discussion: Ibrahim Khan: Requested we make it explicit in the examples that you should NOT parse JSON on every delta, and that deltas may split tokens arbitrarily. Also asked for a test that interleaves deltas between two tool calls. Sabrina James: Added a comment block in both examples (“Do not json.loads incremental deltas; wait until tool call is finalized”) and added test_tool_args_accumulator_interleaving(). Brian Murphy: Asked for error naming consistency with gateway errors (schema mismatch vs incomplete args). Suggested making the message actionable: mention that proxies/buffering can lead to truncated streams and recommend setting a request timeout + retry. Sabrina James: Adjusted exception type/message: IncompleteToolArgumentsError now includes “stream ended before tool arguments were complete” and the README troubleshooting section links to timeout guidance (already being updated in PR #490). Marcus Lin: Security feedback: ensure examples do not show executing arbitrary tools, forbid shell/network in sample tools, and avoid logging full tool args. Requested explicit allowlist and a redaction pattern. Sabrina James: Kept tools minimal (pure functions: get_weather, convert_units) and added allowlist dict + explicit unknown-tool failure path. Redacted tail snippet in errors; examples print only tool name + tool_call_id by default. CI: Initial run failed ruff (unused import in parallel example) and was fixed in the last commit. Current status: all checks green. Merge plan: squash on approval; no version bump in this PR (tracked in release coordination).
